name: Service debugging — Production
description: Production service debugging with logs, trace-ID log correlation, Kubernetes resources and API incident metrics. Rolling last 15 minutes; refresh every 30 seconds. Default: store-api / default / servers-usc1-prd-cluster. Cluster, namespace and deployment scope all workload panels. Pod scopes log and resource panels; severity scopes the log table; Trace ID scopes log investigation only. API route scopes application HTTP metrics only; gateway panels use <deployment>-service. No production stored-span source is configured: trace investigation shows correlated logs, not spans or a service topology. Missing telemetry stays unavailable. See Scope and first checks for rate windows and triage guidance. Includes HPA current/target metrics and min/max/desired/current replicas, a desired/running/ready/available pod comparison, and visible per-pod restarts. Log tables explicitly default to timestamp DESC; arbitrary-column sorting still operates across the selected range. Capacity delivery distinguishes created, scheduled, Running pod phase, running application containers and Ready; includes pending reasons, age, hosting-node registration, 2m gateway RPM and 5m restarts, with incident evidence links.

config.name: App worst route P95 / P99 · 5m histogram
Scope and first checks
config.markdown:
**Scope:** Cluster / Namespace / Deployment drive incident panels. Deployment maps to the app container and `<deployment>-service` ingress destination. Gateway queries retain unknown backends and use the ingress reporter’s cluster. API route filters application HTTP charts only; Pod, Log level and Trace ID do not narrow incident metrics. Route legends include team / subteam / tier.

**Windows:** Rates and histogram percentiles use rolling 5m; failure counts and worst P99 use rolling 15m, even when the displayed time range changes. Counts are counter-increase estimates, not users. Worst P99 is the maximum route P99 sampled each minute. Reporting endpoints count exported route/ownership combinations; active endpoints require positive request rate. Charts display up to 20 series. Empty telemetry stays unavailable; percentages require positive traffic. Missing 4xx/5xx series become zero only where matching request telemetry exists.

**First checks:** **UH** → healthy endpoints, readiness, available replicas and pending pods. **UF / URX** → connection failures, exhausted retries, saturation and reachability. **UT / UO** → timeouts, overload and latency. **UC** → terminated connections, rollouts, draining, restarts and OOM. Check CPU throttling, readiness and replicas in Infrastructure details. HTTP **0 / DC** is a separate no-response signal and is excluded from 5xx totals.

**Alerting guidance:** alert on aggregate 5xx impact with a traffic floor or SLO burn rate, regardless of flag. Flags guide diagnosis, not incident severity. Replica deficits and latency can warn before 5xx; HPA maximum alone is insufficient. This dashboard does not install alerts.

**Trace coverage:** Production currently has no configured stored-span source. The Trace-ID log investigation tabs show logs with correlation IDs. They cannot provide span duration, a waterfall or service topology without ingested spans and a configured trace source.

**HPA and pods:** HPA panels follow the selected Deployment through its scale-target reference, even when the HPA has a different name. HPA min/max/desired/current cards are totals across matching HPAs. Trends retain each HPA. Current metrics are paired only with the configured metric name and target type: utilization is percent of requested resources; average/value use the metric’s native units. Pods desired/running/ready/available compares the whole selected deployment, independent of the Pod filter. Running does not imply Ready. Available replicas satisfy the Deployment availability criteria. Pod restarts sum container restart-counter increases over a rolling 15m; estimates can be fractional.

**Log sorting:** Log tables default to newest first. Column-header sorting queries all matching logs in the selected time range; a 200-row page limit does not limit the scan. Sorting by another column disables incremental time-window fetching. Keep timestamp order for live debugging; for an arbitrary-column investigation, pause Live and select a short time range plus a workload/pod filter. No logs are sampled or discarded by this dashboard.

Capacity diagnosis and incident evidence
config.markdown:
**Scope:** All charts in this section use the selected Cluster / Namespace / Deployment. Pod, API route, severity and trace filters do not narrow this section. Application-container charts match the container name to the deployment name. Nodes are those hosting the selected workload, not the entire cluster.

**Read the gaps:** Desired > Created: controller/pod creation. Created > Scheduled: scheduling. Scheduled > Running: initialization/startup. Running pods > Running app containers: containers stopped or restarting. Running > Ready: health-check failure or startup. Pending includes both unscheduled and already scheduled pods; use the waiting-reason chart and events to distinguish them. Oldest pending age includes all time since creation, not measured scheduler or image-download latency.

**Counting:** Pod states use ReplicaSet ownership and exclude terminating/terminal pods; duplicate scrape series are deduplicated. Deployment Created/Ready/Available use controller status. Rollout surge can exceed Desired. Restart estimates include recently removed pods, use a rolling 5m window and may be fractional. Sparse waiting/error series stay unavailable rather than being fabricated as zeros. A Running pod is not necessarily healthy.

**Timing:** RPM uses a trailing 2m window, while replica counts are sampled states. Do not divide rolling RPM by an instantaneous ready count as measured per-pod throughput. Metric collection can lag events and miss short scheduling failures. Newly registered nodes prove node registration, not that the cloud autoscaler was the cause of creation; confirm the event log.

**Incident evidence · 12 September 2026 (IST):** At 8:33 PM: 57 desired/created/scheduled, 35 Running, 2 Ready. At 8:40: 63 Running, 15 Ready. At 10:08: 100 Running, 8 Ready. First 22 added pods were scheduled in 12–52 seconds on newly registered nodes. Pod 6vj9z's pull step took 4m45.39s including waiting; only 269ms was reported as pull execution. This exact duration comes from GKE events, not these metrics.
